boarders_approx: Not published on the site; two historic houses taking Years 7-13 (Barnicoat also houses Prep boys). About 80+ boarders play a winter sport code (May 2026 newsletter), so the total is likely 120-180 (estimate)
alt_email: boarding@nelson.school.nz (boarding office, on the enrol page); ce@nelson.school.nz (Mark Cochrane, Rutherford House Housemaster, also Assistant Sports Co-ordinator and PE teacher, a good cc for rugby coaching); rc@nelson.school.nz (Ronni Cullen, Boarding Administrator)
gap_notes: No public mention of gap tutors or gappies on the Nelson College site or in search results. Live-in staff are mostly teachers. The large boys' boarding operation with Year 7-13 boarders is a plausible fit for a cold approach.
rugby_notes: A leading South Island rugby school, one of NZ's oldest rugby schools (first NZ club game 1870). 2024 was its most successful 1st XV season: Miles Toyota Premiership, South Island champions and national Top 4 runners-up. In 2026 it plays the Tasman Miles Toyota 1st XV Boys' Premiership plus the new South Island boys' 1st XV competition against CBHS, St Andrew's and others. All Black old boys include Leicester Fainga'anuku.
scenery_notes: Nelson is NZ's sunniest city. Abel Tasman National Park, Golden Bay, Kahurangi and Nelson Lakes are nearby, with beaches, mountain biking, and skiing at Rainbow/Mt Robert. The site mentions beach trips and ski days for boarders.
notes: Both nelson.school.nz and the older nelsoncollege.school.nz domain appear on the site. Use @nelson.school.nz, the current domain in the May 2026 newsletter. The staff email pattern is two-letter initials (first letter of first name + last letter of surname, e.g. mn = Mardon, ce = Cochrane). Emphasise rugby coaching and Economics/Maths tutoring, since Mardon teaches Commerce.

rugby_notes: Plays in the Tasman/Nelson Bays secondary schools rugby scene. Not a national-tier rugby school. Only the boys' house (28) would be relevant for rugby mentoring.
scenery_notes: Richmond sits at the foot of the Richmond Ranges, close to Rabbit Island beach, the Great Taste Trail cycleway, Abel Tasman and Kahurangi. The hostel site mentions beach trips, river adventures and winter ski days.
notes: The hostel is at 1-5 Monro Place, Richmond. Address the email to Robert Booth at hostel@garincollege.nz. It is a Catholic faith-based school.

boarding_houses: Boarding hostel for up to 190 across five buildings in two house identities. The boarding staff page lists Heads of Moyes House, Carrington House and Niger House. Note: Barak, Hatherly, Syme and Donnelly are the school's day-school houses, not boarding houses; the brief's 'Barak House' is not a boarding house.
contact_title: Director of Boarding (since Term 4 2023; also Director of Hockey)
alt_email: office@npbhs.school.nz (main office). Heads of house: Leighton Price (Moyes), Liam Younger (Carrington), Noho Robinson (Niger), no emails published
gap_notes: No public mention of gap tutors. Housemasters are resident teaching staff. With ~190 boarders and 5 house masters plus 2 matrons it is a big operation where an extra resident assistant could be valued. A cold approach is worthwhile.
rugby_notes: A founding Super 8 school (1997) and one of NZ's premier rugby schools. Super 8 1st XV champions in 2015 and 2020, runners-up in 2013, 2019 and 2021, and a regular contender for the national Top 4. It has produced many All Blacks and has its own ground, The Gully.
scenery_notes: Mt Taranaki / Egmont National Park, Surf Highway 45 surfing, Coastal Walkway, and Pouakai Crossing. Outdoor Education is offered and the school has surfing, sailing, snowsports and mountain biking codes.
